<Rep. Mike Thompson>: Mr. Chairman, first I would like to thank my Republican colleague, Representative Fong, for his partnership on this issue. This is how the legislative process should work: Democrats and Republicans coming together to solve real problems for the people we serve. For nine decades, Social Security has done exactly what it has promised, protecting workers, retirees, people with disabilities, and saving families from poverty. Because it is so successful, our job here should be to make it easier, not harder, for Americans to participate and benefit from Social Security.
Under current law, clergy can opt out of paying Social Security taxes if they choose not to receive the benefits when they retire. Our clergy members are pillars of every community, providing spiritual and emotional guidance in times of joy and times of hardship. My Clergy Act would provide members of the clergy a two-year window to opt back in, pay their Social Security taxes, and secure these earned benefits.
But if we are going to make Social Security work better for the American people, we must double down on protecting it from those who wish to tear it down. We cannot talk about strengthening this program on one hand while ignoring ongoing efforts on the other side to weaken it or to privatize it. Repeatedly, we have heard proposals from our Republican colleagues who have called for reforms or ``tough choices.'' Let us be honest about what that means: cuts to benefits, delayed retirement, a move to privatization, and undermining guaranteed benefits that generations have come to count on.
Democrats reject that proposal; we believe Social Security is a promise, not a bargaining chip. In this committee, we have a choice. We can work together to ensure Social Security remains strong for generations to come, or we can go down the road of cuts and uncertainty that jeopardizes the retirement security of millions of Americans. I believe we should make sure Social Security stands strong for future generations.
Mike Thompson.
